title: Indian Women Win Eight of Thirteen Gold Medals at Glasgow Commonwealth Games
excerpt: Women boxers swept five gold medals on a single day while Mirabai Chanu completed a historic CWG hat-trick as India finished with 39 medals in Glasgow.
body:
• Indian women won 8 of the country's 13 gold medals at CWG 2026, with five women boxers sweeping gold on the penultimate day in Glasgow.
  • Mirabai Chanu became the first woman weightlifter to win three consecutive Commonwealth Games gold medals, setting new Games records in the process.
  • India finished fourth overall with 39 medals (13 gold, 17 silver, 9 bronze) despite competing in a scaled-down Games featuring only 10 sports.

Women Boxers Lead a Golden Surge

India's women athletes delivered a definitive statement at the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, winning 8 of the country's 13 gold medals and establishing themselves as the driving force behind Team India's campaign. The most devastating display came from the boxing ring, where five Indian women claimed gold on August 1 in a single-day sweep at the SEC Centre.

Sakshi Chaudhary (51 kg), Preeti Panwar (54 kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57 kg), Priya Ghanghas (60 kg), and Arundhati Choudhary (70 kg) all won their finals by unanimous decisions, according to results published by the Glasgow 2026 Organising Committee. All five had entered Glasgow as reigning Asian Boxing Championships medal winners, with Preeti, Priya, and Arundhati carrying gold from the continental event in Ulaanbaatar in April.

Boxing was India's most successful discipline at these Games, yielding 7 of the country's 13 golds. The remaining two boxing golds went to Sachin Siwach (men's 60 kg) and Ankush Panghal (men's 80 kg). Lovlina Borgohain, the Tokyo Olympics bronze medallist who served as India's baton-bearer at the opening ceremony, added a silver in the women's 75 kg category.

"This is my third gold medal at the Commonwealth Games. I am extremely happy. I can't express how happy I am to win my third gold medal."

— Mirabai Chanu, Weightlifter

Chanu Completes Historic Hat-Trick

Weightlifter Mirabai Chanu set the tone for India's women early in the Games, winning the country's first gold of Glasgow 2026 on July 26 in the women's 48 kg category. Competing at the SEC Armadillo, Chanu lifted a combined 190 kg — 85 kg in snatch and 105 kg in clean and jerk — breaking Games records in both disciplines, according to the Sporting News.

The Manipuri lifter finished 22 kg ahead of Nigeria's Ruth Asuquo Nyong, who took silver with 168 kg. The gold made Chanu the first woman weightlifter to win three consecutive CWG titles, following her triumphs at Gold Coast 2018 and Birmingham 2022. It was also her fourth CWG medal overall, counting a silver from Glasgow 2014 — the city where her Commonwealth career began.

Gold Beyond the Ring and the Platform

India's women contributed gold in judo and para athletics as well. Asmita Dey won the women's 48 kg judo title on July 31, while Sharmila Dhankar became India's first-ever para-athletics gold medallist at the Commonwealth Games with her victory in the women's shot put F57 event on July 27, according to the Latestly.

Women added four silvers — Gyaneshwari Yadav in weightlifting 53 kg, Harjinder Kaur in weightlifting 69 kg, Yamini Mourya in judo 57 kg, and Lovlina Borgohain in boxing 75 kg — and four bronzes from Bindyarani Devi in weightlifting 58 kg, Shilpa Shyla in para shot put, Seema Kaliramna in discus throw, and Unnati Sharma in judo 63 kg. In total, women accounted for 16 of India's 39 medals — and 8 of the 13 golds.

A Scaled-Down Games, But a Focused Campaign

India sent 122 athletes — 75 men and 47 women — to compete across 10 disciplines in Glasgow. The 2026 edition was significantly smaller than Birmingham 2022, which featured 19 sports. Historically productive events for India like badminton, hockey, squash, table tennis, and wrestling were all dropped from the programme, according to the Sporting News.

India won 61 medals in Birmingham. The reduced slate made matching that total unrealistic, but India's 39-medal haul with a fourth-place ranking reflected a focused and efficient campaign. The contingent was led by Chef de Mission Rohit Rajpal, with Mirabai Chanu carrying the flag at the opening ceremony and boxing champion Jaismine Lamboria carrying it at closing — a fitting tribute to the women who defined this campaign.

A Moment for the Diaspora

Glasgow, which hosted the 2014 Commonwealth Games and has a longstanding Indian community in Scotland, provided a familiar stage. For the Indian diaspora in the UK and beyond, the dominance of women athletes offered a visible symbol of the shifting landscape of Indian sport — one where boxers from Haryana, lifters from Manipur, and judokas from across the country carry the national flag on the biggest stages.

What's Next

With the CWG wrapping up on August 2, attention shifts to how India can carry this boxing momentum into the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. The five women boxing gold medallists — all in their early-to-mid twenties — represent a deep pipeline that head coach Santiago Nieva has built through Asian and Commonwealth competition. The question now is whether the programme can sustain this dominance when the competition widens to a global field.
nri_angle: Indian women's dominance at Glasgow CWG resonates with the diaspora community in the UK and globally, symbolizing India's evolving sporting identity.
